question: How did total revenue, operating income and operating margin change over the last three fiscal years?

answer.summary: Total revenue grew steadily over the three-year window, rising from $567.76B in FY2022 [F00005] to $605.88B in FY2023 (+6.7% YoY) [F00004] and $642.64B in FY2024 (+6.1% YoY) [F00003], a 6.4% CAGR and +13% over the window. Operating income was volatile: it fell 21.3% YoY to $20.43B in FY2023 [F00019] from $25.94B in FY2022 [F00020], then rebounded 32.2% to $27.01B in FY2024 [F00018], ending the window +4% above the FY2022 level. Operating margin mirrored this trajectory: 4.6% in FY2022 [F01836], down 120 bps to 3.4% in FY2023 [F01837], then up 83 bps to 4.2% in FY2024 [F01838]. FY2024 revenue growth was driven primarily by Walmart US (58% of the total change) and Walmart International (37%), while FY2024 operating income growth was driven by Corporate And Support's $2.88B improvement (44% of the total change) alongside Walmart International (+30%) and Walmart US (+23%). Net income followed a similar pattern to operating income, falling to $11.29B in FY2023 [F00046] before spiking to $16.27B in FY2024 [F00045].
drivers: Revenue FY2024 change ($36.76B, +6.1%): Walmart US was the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR with $21.26B (+5.1%), accounting for 58% of the total change [F00958]; Walmart International contributed $13.66B (+13.5%), 37% of the total change [F00959]; Sams Club contributed $1.83B (+2.2%), 5% of the total change [F00960].

Operating income FY2024 change ($6.58B, +32.2%): Corporate And Support was the LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR with a $2.88B improvement (from -$5.12B to -$2.24B, -56.2%), accounting for 44% of the total change [F00965]; Walmart International contributed $1.94B (+65.6%), 30% of the total change [F00963]; Walmart US contributed $1.53B (+7.4%), 23% of the total change [F00962].
Operating margin recovery in FY2024 (+83 bps) coincides with operating income growing faster (+32.2%) than revenue (+6.1%), per management text [T00425].
risks_and_red_flags: Operating income declined sharply in FY2023 (-21.3% YoY to $20.43B) [F00019], indicating earnings volatility rather than a smooth growth path.
FY2024 operating margin (4.2%) [F01838] remains below the FY2022 level (4.6%) [F01836], so the margin recovery is incomplete relative to the start of the window.
SG&A expense grew faster than revenue in FY2023 (+7.9% YoY) [F00016] versus revenue (+6.7%) [F00004], a cost-pressure signal that coincides with the FY2023 operating income decline.
Net income spiked 29% vs the prior-2-period average in FY2024 [F00045], which may reflect one-off items rather than recurring profitability.
